abstract: For the Collatz inverse maps $I_e(x)=(2^ex-1)/3$ on the $3$-adic units, retaining unit-valued children and restricting $1\le e\le5$, we prove that the only closed sets containing every legal child of each of their points are the empty set, the forced fixed point $\{1/13\}$, and the whole unit space. Consequently every other unit reaches every prescribed unit residue modulo every power of three with all inverse exponents at most five. This proves the all-precision routing conjecture previously verified through modulus $243$; the corresponding cap-four statement fails because of a known Cantor trap. The proof first combines a uniform three-edge alternative with equal-total affine-word separation to construct a positive-dimensional law on any nontrivial trap. An exact cylinder-entropy identity transfers positive entropy rate to a stationary law of the original uniform legal-child chain. The Haar reverse kernel makes every proper trap uniformly porous. Conditioning on the actual source cylinder and total exponent then expresses a block transition as an independent convolution whose offset entropy grows linearly. A finite cyclic-group entropy gap forces linear convolution gain, contradicting the sublinear stationary entropy budget. All branch probabilities and conditioning costs are retained, and no residue census enters the proof. Compactness also gives a qualitative logarithmic dependence on the input for each fixed target. No effective target-dependent length bound or forward Collatz convergence theorem is claimed.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Collatz inverse routing with exponents at most five at every ternary precision
